high_level_description: The image is a screenshot of a webpage from medium.com, displaying an article about the structure and function of hypercolumns in the brain. The text explains that a hypercolumn extends from the surface of the occipital lobe down into the underlying white matter and is organized into horizontal layers called laminae. It further describes how these laminae receive functional connections from neurons located in a nucleus labeled dLGN (dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus) and how other layers receive inputs from additional brain areas.
